message.text: I recall that connect.ts has an authInterceptor handling the Bearer access token and refresh token cookie, with backend validation happening in the auth package's authenticator.go that I saw earlier.

I need to confirm the token types at play here: access tokens (JWTs, short-lived, sent via Bearer header), refresh tokens (cookie-based, used to mint new access tokens), and Personal Access Tokens. Let me check auth-state.ts to pin down exactly how the frontend manages these.

So the access token stays in memory, while the refresh token lives in an httpOnly cookie handled server-side, with the refresh RPC using credentials: include to send it. That settles the design, so I can finalize the answer.
